messages:
maya: Quick sync — proposing a new region-selection policy before the next hosted API rollout. TL;DR: latency-first for enterprise in-region, cost-fallback for free/dev, and model-variant downgrade if cross-region is too expensive. Need opinions on quotas and telemetry visibility.

jon: +1 for latency-first for enterprise. Question: how do we measure "in-region" latency? p95 over what window?

maya: thinking p95 over 1m for probes + moving 5m average for decision stability. Probe weight should be adjustable per-tenant.

ashwin: if we probe every 30s we're adding load. Can we reuse existing health pings? also we need to avoid oscillation during transient network blips.

leela: agree with ashwin. Add hysteresis: require threshold breach for 2 consecutive windows before switching.

ritesh: on model variants: for non-enterprise tiers we should try quantized 4-bit variant in secondary region first instead of heavy model in primary region. cheaper and keeps latency acceptable.

jon: That reminds me — quota implications. If we route cross-region, egress/cost should bill to tenant and count toward their quota. Do we currently attribute cost by routing region?

maya: Not consistently. Right now cost attribution is model-level + region tag in traces, but not rolled up to the quota service. Need to decide policy: charge tenant for the region they were served from (preferred) or charge original region for accounting simplicity.

ashwin: We should charge by serving region. Simpler for finance and aligns incentives. Implementation: include serving_region in billing events.

leela: UX note: console needs a toggle per-tenant: "allow cross-region fallback" + visible trace of last N routing decisions. Product asks for a compact timeline card, not a big dump.

maya: Good call. New console fields: last_decision, reason, latency_at_switch, model_variant, cost_delta.

ritesh: Also need to expose fallback policy in per-route configs. Example YAML sketch:```yaml
routing:
  tier_policy:
    enterprise:
      prefer_in_region: true
      latency_slo_ms: 150
      allow_cross_region_fallback: false
    standard:
      prefer_in_region: true
      latency_slo_ms: 250
      allow_cross_region_fallback: true
      model_variant_fallback_order: ["optimum", "quantized-4bit", "fast-legacy"]
    dev:
      prefer_in_region: false
      latency_slo_ms: 350
      allow_cross_region_fallback: true
      cost_priority: high
```

jon: That YAML looks fine. One more internal API debate: should routing policy be evaluated in the control plane (centralized) or in the edge routers? Centralized gives consistent decisions and easier telemetry; edge reduces extra RTT.

ashwin: Edge judges better for latency, but then we need to replicate policy and probes everywhere. Centralized easier for rollouts and A/B. Maybe hybrid: central policy decides preferences and probes, edge executes shortcuts based on local probe cache.

maya: Hybrid sounds right. Edge keeps a local decision cache with TTL and fallback to central if unknown. Also record a routing_decision event in our trace pipeline with tags: {tenant, route, serving_region, model_variant, reason}.

leela: On telemetry: please include a boolean field "cross_region" and numeric "decision_penalty_ms" so console can surface expected extra latency vs in-region.

jon: Need to think about quotas: if tenant has commit for dedicated capacity in eu-west, should cross-region fallback to us-east be allowed? That could violate isolation promises.

maya: Good catch. For Dedicated/Private customers with isolation flags, default allow_cross_region_fallback must be false. Add an escape valve for SRE: emergency_failover=true only with audit log.

ritesh: Rollout UX: we want a canary that flips the policy flag for 5% of traffic on standard tier and shows per-tenant impact on cost/latency before full rollout. Console should show a quick compare card.

deploy-bot: canary-config applied to hosted/canary-1987: routing.hybrid=true, canary_fraction=0.05

leela: For observability, add these graphs: regional_p95_by_tenant, fallback_rate_by_tenant, avg_cost_delta_on_fallback. Also add alert if fallback_rate > 5% for enterprise tenants.

jon: How do we surface the "reason" for fallback? e.g., probe_timeout vs capacity_exhausted vs quota_exceeded vs manual_override. We need machine-readable reason codes.

maya: Proposed reason codes: PROBE_HIGH_LATENCY, REGIONAL_CAPACITY, MODEL_INCOMPATIBLE, QUOTA_LIMIT, MANUAL_OVERRIDE, OTHER. Add these to traces and billing events.

ashwin: Implementation plan: 1) decision model + reason codes in control plane API 2) edge local cache + probe adapter 3) billing events include serving_region and reason 4) console cards + telemetry graphs 5) canary rollout.

ritesh: Also add a fallback policy to pick a cheaper model variant in-region before doing cross-region, as a cost-preserving step. That reduces egress and preserves locality.

leela: UX detail: when a tenant toggles allow_cross_region_fallback off, the console should warn about possible latency or error increase and offer to run a simulation for last 24h.

jon: Any performance budget cost for probes? We should include probe budget in tenant config so big tenants don't provoke extra pings.

maya: Agree. Add probe_budget_per_minute per-tenant, with a cluster default. Also make probes sample-based for large tenants.

deploy-bot: canary metrics: fallback_rate=0.8%, avg_decision_latency=12ms, cross_region_calls=120 (last 10m)

leela: Those metrics look healthy so far. Can we wire up a quick dashboard tile in Console > Routes > Canary to show these?

maya: I'll create a short design ticket for the console card. Action items: @jon implement billing event changes; @ashwin spec edge cache + probes; @ritesh add model-variant-first fallback; @leela design console card + simulation; @maya drive canary and policy docs.

jon: I'll start on billing events. Quick question: should billing include estimated egress cost or actual egress cost? finance prefers actual but that requires tagging at egress time.

maya: Actual if possible. If not, approximate with region model pricing table. Note it in docs.

slo-bot: ALERT: enterprise fallback_rate exceeded 5% for tenant "papertrail-inc" at 1987654380 (investigate).

maya: Thanks, @slo-bot — I'll pick that up after this thread.

leela: small UX ask: in the timeline card show the most recent routing_decision JSON snippet (one-liner). Example: `{serving_region: "eu-west-1", model_variant: "optimum", reason: "PROBE_HIGH_LATENCY", decision_penalty_ms: 120}`

maya: perfect. Ok folks — will collate this and post a short RFC. Thanks for the fast takes.

jon: +1, let's get the RFC up today.

ashwin: will draft edge adapter spec tomorrow.

ritesh: I'll prototype model-variant switcher in the runtime branch.

deploy-bot: canary-check ok — no regressions observed in routing logic tests.

maya: End of thread — moving actions to task tracker.
